setting: A fictional review with a project sponsor who wants to act on two reports.

presentation.situation: {{name}}, the project sponsor, says that {{claim}}. Your figures: {{good}}, but also {{bad}}. {{unknown}} Test the assumptions, weigh the evidence, and say what you would do.
presentation.opening: The report says {{claim}}. That proves it's working, so I want to roll it out everywhere. You agree, don't you?

brief.you_are: You are an analyst reviewing evidence with a project sponsor.
brief.situation: {{name}}, the project sponsor, says that {{claim}}. Your figures: {{good}}, but also {{bad}}. {{unknown}} Test the assumptions, weigh the evidence, and say what you would do.
brief.task: Question the assumption, weigh both pieces of evidence, and give a reasoned judgement on what to do next.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} sees why the conclusion is not yet safe, and has a clear recommendation from you.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are an analyst reviewing evidence with a project sponsor.
goals: Question the assumption, weigh both pieces of evidence, and give a reasoned judgement on what to do next.

card.want: To make a quick decision that can be defended.
card.hidden_need: Promised the board an update this month.
card.attitude: Keen, in a hurry, and fair when shown evidence.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

objectives.evidence: The learner questions an assumption, or looks for alternative explanations.
alternatives: That assumes the change caused it. Could something else explain it?

objectives.evidence: The learner uses both pieces of evidence.
alternatives: The data shows one thing improved, but the other got worse.

objectives.evidence: The learner makes a reasoned recommendation.
alternatives: I recommend a small test before rolling out, because the evidence is mixed.

examples: That assumes the change caused it. Could something else explain it?
The data shows one figure improved, but the other got worse.
I recommend a small test first, because the evidence is mixed.

opportunity: So you agree that it is working?
What is wrong with that conclusion?
beats.orient: I've jumped to a conclusion. Question it. You can ask: Could something else explain it?
fallback: What is wrong with that conclusion?
So you agree that it is working?

opportunity: What does the data actually tell us?
beats.orient: Look at both figures in your brief. Tell me what they show together.
fallback: What does the data actually tell us?

opportunity: I need a decision. What do you recommend?
beats.orient: Now tell me what you would do, and why. Start with: I recommend.
fallback: I need a decision. What do you recommend?

closing_line: Fair enough. That's a stronger position than the one I walked in with.

o1.good: Asking what else could explain the result.
o1.micro_lesson: Ask: What are we assuming? What else could explain it?
o1.model: That assumes the change caused it. Could something else explain it?
o1.smaller_step: Ask: Could something else explain it?

o2.good: Looking at all the evidence, including what doesn't fit.
o2.micro_lesson: Say: The data shows, and: but.
o2.model: The data shows one figure improved, but the other got worse.

o3.good: A clear decision, even with incomplete evidence.
common_mistakes: Saying only: We need more data
o3.model: I recommend a small test first, because the evidence is mixed.

variants.name: Zara
variants.claim: the new training raised sales by 10 percent
variants.good: sales rose by 10 percent in the trained team
variants.unknown: A seasonal promotion ran at the same time, and nobody has separated its effect.

variants.name: Andrew
variants.claim: the new system improved response times by 20 percent
variants.good: average response time improved by 20 percent
variants.unknown: The team also reduced the number of questions it answers per ticket.
